analyst_view.overall: Second-placed Brighton (22 points, six wins in their last seven league games, each with a clean sheet) visit 13th-placed Hull (11 points), who are eight league games without a win but have never lost at home to Brighton in six meetings at the MKM Stadium. Jakirovic says Belloumi and Nobel Mendy are completely fine after the international break and Crooks is available, while Targett, Matazo, Hughes, Morita and Ansah stay out, as the numbers assume. Brighton have Gross (who signed a new contract on Friday), Kadioglu, Chema, Struijk and Hadjam available, with Minteh likely only a substitute after just eight minutes against Brentford; Mitoma, Ferguson, Yohanna and Tzimas are out and already counted. Expect Hull in a compact 5-4-1, playing direct to McBurnie with about a third of the ball, against Brighton's patient possession game; Hurzeler warned that Hull are good in transition. Referee Peter Bankes averages 4.0 cards a game, the league average, which the numbers count, and since the latest team news matches what the numbers assumed I keep every stat where they put it.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals (Hull 1.0, Brighton 1.4), already trimming Hull a little for scoring only 6 in their last six. Brighton's run of clean sheets and Hull's low-scoring home draws point to a tight game, but that form is in the ratings, and Mitoma, Ferguson and Tzimas being out is already taken off Brighton, so I stay at 2.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, already adding a little for Hull's recent rise (31 corners in six). Minteh is fit but expected only off the bench and Mitoma is out, as the numbers assume, and Hull's 5-4-1 with Giles and Coyle as wing-backs is their usual shape, so I stay at 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, already counting Brighton's busier recent card count (16 in six) and referee Peter Bankes, who averages 4.0 a game. Jakirovic wants Hull to match Brighton's aggressive pressing and Crooks is back to battle Gross in midfield, but nothing points to a heated game beyond what the numbers see, so I stay at 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.0 shots, already adding about 8% to Brighton for their high recent output (102 shots in six). Previews have Brighton at around 17 shots a game against Hull's nine, which is what the ratings already show, and Brighton's line-up is at full strength rather than stronger than usual, so I keep 27.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target, already lowering Hull's for poor recent accuracy (16 on target in six). Belloumi, Hull's main creator, is fit as the numbers assumed, and Brighton's attack around Gross and Kostoulas is as expected without Mitoma, so I stay at 8.2.
